concerns: Spike-in tracer behavior may not mirror endogenous EVs (proposal notes this risk) and could produce false assurance if spike-in recovery drives apparent concordance rather than endogenous signals (needs orthogonal controls to exclude).

Assay harmonization across sites is challenging (platform differences, capture-compatibility, particle counters) and may generate false discordance; proposal dependence on SOP harmonization is a program risk supported by MISEV recommendations.

Co-isolation of non-vesicular components could produce consistent but spurious composite fingerprints (MISEV warns about separation/identity confounders); the proposal must ensure orthogonal separation and negative controls to rule this out.
Pilot-lot count (≥3) and site count (≥2) are minimal; statistical robustness and sensitivity to detect meaningful lot variability may require more lots/sites or repeatability assessment.
No human clinical evidence is cited (only preclinical rodent/NHP findings); translational risks (biodistribution/species differences) remain and support cautious interpretation (ev-driedonks-2022).
conclusion: Supported in principle by the cited canonical evidence (MISEV2023 guidance for orthogonal characterization; program rodent evidence for protected-cargo/identity relevance; NHP biodistribution caution), but the core claim—that a composite, spike-in–validated qualitative fingerprint will be reproducibly measurable across ≥3 pilot lots and ≥2 sites—lacks direct empirical support in the supplied evidence and therefore requires the proposed blinded multi-lot, multi-site experiment to close the gap.
evidence_gap: No direct experimental evidence demonstrating blinded, multi-lot, multi-site reproducible detection of the proposed composite fingerprint (spike-in validated) across independent pilot lots and analytical sites; i.e., the key multi-site reproducibility experiment is missing.
